title: Separate movement intent from attack facing
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: Directional combat with persistent airborne facing. Grounded-only facing is a design-specific correction, not a universal control rule; physical gamepad feel was not established.
goal: Select front and backward aerial attacks relative to character facing.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Movement direction was used to update orientation before interpreting attack intent.
what_worked: Historical correction: Under this game's rules, update facing from grounded movement only and retain the airborne attack reference frame. Verification reported by the source: Five aerial attack variants were rechecked through actual Input Actions after correction.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Opposite horizontal input immediately flipped facing in air, so backward aerial attack could not be selected.
why: Confirmed: the reference frame changed in response to the same input that was meant to select the backward attack.
improved_method: Specify whether directional input changes orientation or selects an action relative to existing orientation. Test opposite input after takeoff before classifying the attack.
when_to_use: Directional combat with persistent airborne facing. Grounded-only facing is a design-specific correction, not a universal control rule; physical gamepad feel was not established.
when_not_to_use: Grounded-only facing is a design-specific correction, not a universal control rule; physical gamepad feel was not established.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
